platform_notes: # Application.Windows property (Excel)

--- title: Application.Windows property (Excel) keywords: vbaxl10.chm183114 f1_keywords: - vbaxl10.chm183114 api_name: - Excel.Application.Windows ms.assetid: 07e54620-c2f5-2354-f313-9756a0f17425 ms.date: 04/05/2019 ms.localizationpriority: medium ---
Returns a **[Windows](Excel.Windows.md)** collection that represents all the windows in all the workbooks. Read-only **Windows** object.
This example names window one in the active workbook Consolidated Balance Sheet. This name is then used as the index to the **Windows** collection.
This property returns a collection of both visible and hidden windows.
Using this property without an object qualifier is equivalent to using Application.Windows.
_expression_.**Windows**
```vb ActiveWorkbook.Windows(1).Caption = "Consolidated Balance Sheet" ActiveWorkbook.Windows("Consolidated Balance Sheet") _ .ActiveSheet.Calculate ```
```vb Application.Windows(1).Close ```

To return a single **ProtectedViewWindow** object from the **[ProtectedViewWindows](Excel.ProtectedViewWindows.md)** collection, use **ProtectedViewWindows** (_index_), where _index_ is the index number of the window that you want to open.

Workbooks displayed in a Protected View window cannot be edited and are restricted from running active content such as Visual Basic for Applications macros and data connections. For more information about Protected View windows, see [What is Protected View?](https://support.office.com/article/what-is-protected-view-d6f09ac7-e6b9-4495-8e43-2bbcdbcb6653?ocmsassetID=HA010355931&CTT=1&CorrelationId=ad189265-115e-4f59-bdf0-ee99038a5bb0&ui=en-US&rs=en-US&ad=US)

```vb MsgBox "There are " & ProtectedViewWindows.Count & _ " Protected View windows currently open." ```

The name of the specified range.

This must be an A1-style reference in the language the macro is written in.

It can include:
  • The range operator (a colon).
  • The intersection operator (a space).
  • The union operator (a comma).
It can also include dollar signs, but they're ignored.

platform_notes: Many worksheet characteristics, such as scroll bars and gridlines, are actually properties of the window. The **Window** object is a member of the **[Windows](Excel.Windows.md)** collection.
Note that the active window is always `Windows(1)`.

The **Windows** collection for the **[Application](Excel.Application(object).md)** object contains all the windows in the application, whereas the **Windows** collection for the **[Workbook](Excel.Workbook.md)** object contains only the windows in the specified workbook.

The window caption is the text shown in the title bar at the top of the window when the window isn't maximized. The caption is also shown in the list of open files on the bottom of the **Windows** menu. Use the **Caption** property to set or return the window caption. Changing the window caption doesn't change the name of the workbook.
Use **[Windows](excel.application.windows.md)** (_index_), where _index_ is the window name or index number, to return a single **Window** object. The following example maximizes the active window.
```vb Windows("book1.xls":1).DisplayGridlines = False ```
```vb Windows(1).WindowState = xlMaximized ```

platform_notes: # Workbook.Windows property (Excel)

--- title: Workbook.Windows property (Excel) keywords: vbaxl10.chm199165 f1_keywords: - vbaxl10.chm199165 api_name: - Excel.Workbook.Windows ms.assetid: 2352d6c9-720e-b58d-6e7c-049bf21a090d ms.date: 05/29/2019 ms.localizationpriority: medium ---
Returns a **[Windows](Excel.Windows.md)** collection that represents all the windows in the specified workbook. Read-only **Windows** object.
This example names window one in the active workbook Consolidated Balance Sheet. This name is then used as the index to the **Windows** collection.
This property returns a collection of both visible and hidden windows.
Using this property without an object qualifier is equivalent to using **Application.Windows**.
_expression_.**Windows**
```vb ActiveWorkbook.Windows(1).Caption = "Consolidated Balance Sheet" ActiveWorkbook.Windows("Consolidated Balance Sheet") _ .ActiveSheet.Calculate ```

By default, January 1, 1900 is serial number 1, and January 1, 2008 is serial number 39448 because it is 39,448 days after January 1, 1900.
